turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: What brings you in?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I'm just coming in with my son, he's been having, he's been complaining of just, seems like pain in his right ear for the last I would say three to four days. And it seems like he's just more irritable, just not himself right now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah OK, so, how long did you say he's had this ear pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: I would say four days now.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Four days, OK. Have you noticed any hearing loss?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, he still responds when I call his name.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and, have you noticed any fluid coming out of his ears?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Is it more like one side of his ears or is it both ears?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It's just his right ear.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Just his right ear, OK. And have you noticed that it's like, swollen, red or warm?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, I don't see any swelling or redness at all.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, good, and have you taken a look inside his ears?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I tried to take a look with a flashlight. I couldn't really see too much.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, yeah, that's fair. And you mentioned he's had a runny nose too, When did that start?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so that, kind of like last week he was recovering from, I think it was just a cold and he had a runny nose and just was a bit congested. But then over the last week it kind of just resolved. But then this week he started having just this ear pain.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. Any fevers?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, not that I, I haven't measured anything and he hasn't mentioned any, like he hasn't felt cold or anything like that.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any weight loss over the past month or so?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, any change in his hair or nails, like rashes or, sorry, or skin?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, no, I haven't seen any changes in the skin.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, any changes in his vision or smell or taste?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK. His runny nose, what color is it?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: It was mainly, uh, it seemed to me like it was mainly clear when it was happening, like he wasn't bringing up any yellow or green material.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, good. Does he have a sore throat at all?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, not that he's told me. He's still eating things and I don't think he's having any trouble with eating anything, so I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, that's good. Has he had a cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, actually he did. He did start coughing like yesterday, but just a few times a day. I don't know if it's because of this or like, what else might be going on.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and you said for the past few days, he's had the cough?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I think just maybe started yesterday.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Started yesterday, OK. Is it a dry cough or is it, is he bringing up any phlegm?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, it seems to be just dry. I think I just noticed it like three or four times during the day yesterday.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, so no blood that he's bringing up right?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, and does he have any shortness of breath?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK, any wheezing?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no wheezing.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No chest pain?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, uhm, any nausea or vomiting?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No nausea or vomiting.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any changes to his bowel movements?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK and, how about urine, is that normal?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, Uh, no changes at all.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Any headaches?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not that he's told me about.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, dizziness or fainting spells?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Feeling like he's off balance or lost coordination?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I don't think so.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: No, OK, no numbness, no tingling?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Has he had any contacts with sick people recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uhm, no, I don't think anyone's been sick around him.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK and has he traveled to anywhere recently?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh, no, like, he's mainly just been inside his home.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK. has he ever had ear pain before?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: He did have a similar pain, I think when he was like around three years old, but it happened with his left left ear, not the right one.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, was he prescribed any medications?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh yeah, he was given a, like a course of antibiotics at that time. I forgot what it was called, but I think at that time it was much worse, like he, I don't know if he was just younger and couldn't tolerate it but I think he also had a fever at that time.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, and then any other ear infections outside of that one time.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, I think that, only that one I can recall.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, alright, is he otherwise healthy?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, otherwise he's healthy. No, other conditions or anything like that.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Not that we know of so far.

turns.text: And any family history of lung conditions or heart conditions.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, how old was he when was diagnosed with celiac?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Fairly young I would say, in his 20s.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, uhm, alright, we'll keep an eye on it in him, like if he has any changes in his bowel movements or if he's getting severe abdominal pain after eating certain foods with gluten you can get him checked up for that as well.

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: OK.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah and then, in terms of where he lives, does he live with you and your partner?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, so it's just, he's an only child, lives with me and my husband, and also we have like a pet dog.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, do you live in an apartment or in a house?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: We live in a, it's like a condominium.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, OK, any old carpet, mold or asbestos in the building?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no, nothing like that. It's fairly well kept.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, And is he other-wise like developmental-wise, he's OK? There's no past history of like developmental disorders, anything like that?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: No, no issues from like when he was younger like no complaints at all. I Think he was doing the same as every other child.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, no complications during your pregnancy with him, no complications during the actual delivery and then when he was a newborn?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Uh no, no complications, it was just a vaginal birth at 39 weeks and we didn't need to stay in the hospital at all afterwards.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK, good. So those were all the questions that I had for you today. Did you have any questions of your own?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, I don't know if, uh, like last time we did get some antibiotics. I don't know if he needs them right now or what would you recommend?

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: Yeah, uhm so I'm gonna have to take a look into his ears first before I can come up with like a management plan for him. So once I do, if I see, uhm, if his tympanic membrane has been perforated or I see pus in there, we'll prescribe him like 10 days of antibiotics. We can give him either Amoxicillin, or if he has bad reactions to penicillins,  we can give him Cefuroxime and then if, uh, it doesn't seem to have any systemic symptoms, so if he has systemic symptoms like fever, which we'll check for today, and if he's like been really ill and he has like a middle ear effusion or bulging tympanic membrane, again we'll give him antibiotics for 10 days. But if his tympanic membrane is just bulging a little bit, or if he has some middle ear effusion but no systemic symptoms, like, no fevers, and he seems to be fine otherwise, we'll reassess him in 24 to 48 hours to see if he's better and if he's not, again, will prescribe him antibiotics. How does that sound?

turns.label: Patient
turns.text: Yeah, that sounds good. Thank you.

turns.label: Clinician
turns.text: OK yeah, no worries.
